source.name: ASTRA Bio wave 1 — Photosynthesis in Higher Plants
source.license: Original syllabus-based practice questions (exam-frequent themes; not verbatim past papers)

questions.stem: van Niel inferred that photosynthetic oxygen comes from water by studying
questions.explanation: Purple sulphur bacteria use H2S, not H2O; van Niel generalised that higher plants split water.

questions.stem: The stroma of the chloroplast is mainly the site of
options: splitting of water by PS II
questions.explanation: Calvin-cycle enzymes are dissolved in the stroma; light reactions sit on thylakoids.

questions.stem: The essential reaction-centre pigment of green plants is
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll a is the reaction-centre pigment; chlorophyll b and carotenoids are accessory.

questions.stem: The reaction centre of photosystem II is designated
questions.explanation: PS II reaction-centre chlorophyll a absorbs maximally near 680 nm; PS I is P700.

questions.stem: Non-cyclic photophosphorylation yields
questions.explanation: Electrons flow from water through PS II and PS I to NADP+, making NADPH and ATP.

questions.stem: The oxygen-evolving complex that splits water is associated with
questions.explanation: Water is split on the lumen side of PS II, releasing O2, electrons and protons.

questions.stem: The enzyme that carboxylates RuBP in the Calvin cycle is
questions.explanation: RuBisCO adds CO2 to ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate, forming two molecules of 3-PGA.

questions.stem: Kranz anatomy with large bundle-sheath chloroplasts is typical of
questions.explanation: C4 leaves show a wreath of bundle-sheath cells around veins (Kranz anatomy).

questions.stem: Photorespiration is favoured when RuBisCO binds
questions.explanation: Oxygenase activity of RuBisCO starts the C2 cycle and wastes carbon as CO2.

questions.stem: Blackman’s law of limiting factors states that the rate is set by
options: the factor present in least supply
the factor present in greatest supply
questions.explanation: When several factors act, the one nearest its minimum controls the rate.

questions.stem: Cyclic photophosphorylation involves
options: both PS II and photolysis of water
only photosystem I and produces ATP
questions.explanation: Electrons cycle around PS I; ATP is made but NADPH and O2 are not.

questions.stem: The primary CO2 acceptor in mesophyll cells of C4 plants is
questions.explanation: PEP carboxylase fixes CO2 onto PEP in mesophyll; the C3 acceptor RuBP is used later in bundle sheath.

questions.stem: To make one glucose in the Calvin cycle the chloroplast typically uses
questions.explanation: Six CO2 require 18 ATP and 12 NADPH (3 ATP and 2 NADPH per CO2).

questions.stem: Engelmann’s Cladophora action-spectrum experiment showed bacteria gathering mainly in
questions.explanation: Aerobic bacteria clustered where O2 was released, matching chlorophyll’s blue and red peaks.

questions.stem: Thylakoid membranes of the chloroplast house
questions.explanation: PS II, the cytochrome b6f complex, PS I and ATP synthase are membrane proteins of the thylakoid.

questions.stem: Accessory pigments help photosynthesis chiefly by
options: absorbing light and passing energy to chlorophyll a
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll b and carotenoids broaden the harvest of wavelengths and protect the reaction centre.

questions.stem: In the Z-scheme, electrons lost by PS II are replaced by electrons from
questions.explanation: Photolysis of water donates electrons to P680 after it has reduced the chain toward PS I.

questions.stem: ATP formed on the thylakoid is synthesised by
options: ATP synthase driven by a proton gradient
questions.explanation: Mitchell chemiosmosis: protons flow back through CF0–CF1 ATP synthase into the stroma.

questions.stem: Protons released during photolysis of water accumulate mainly in the
questions.explanation: The oxygen-evolving complex faces the lumen, so photolysis acidifies that space.

questions.stem: The first stable product of CO2 fixation in C3 plants is
questions.explanation: RuBisCO + RuBP yields two 3-carbon 3-PGA molecules; OAA is the C4 first product.

questions.stem: The Hatch–Slack pathway first fixes CO2 in the
questions.explanation: Mesophyll PEP carboxylase makes a C4 acid that is then shipped to the bundle sheath.

questions.stem: Photorespiration is considered wasteful because it
options: releases CO2 without making ATP or sugar
questions.explanation: The C2 cycle consumes O2 and ATP-equivalent energy and loses carbon as CO2.

questions.stem: If light is already saturating, a further rise in C3 photosynthesis is often limited by
questions.explanation: Once light is plentiful, CO2 (and sometimes temperature) becomes the limiting factor.

questions.stem: Which statement about early photosynthesis work is incorrect?
options: Priestley showed a mint plant could restore air
Sachs found glucose/starch in green parts
Engelmann proved CO2 is released by mitochondria
questions.explanation: Engelmann mapped the action spectrum of O2 release; he did not study mitochondrial CO2.

questions.stem: CAM plants open stomata and do the initial CO2 fixation mainly
questions.explanation: Night-time PEP carboxylase stores C4 acids; stomata stay shut by day to save water.

questions.stem: During non-cyclic electron flow, which sequence is correct?
options: PS I → water → PS II → NADP+
Water → PS II → cyt b6f → PS I → NADP+
NADP+ → PS I → PS II → water
questions.explanation: The Z-scheme runs from water through PS II and the cytochrome complex to PS I and then NADP+.
